questions.scenario: An organisation needs a model to answer questions using internal engineering documents, with citations to the source. Which approach?
options: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases
questions.explain: RAG retrieves the relevant documents at query time, which both grounds the answer and makes source citation possible. Fine-tuning absorbs knowledge into weights and cannot cite sources.

questions.scenario: Which sequence correctly orders FM customisation approaches from LOWEST to HIGHEST cost?
questions.explain: Prompt engineering is free beyond tokens, RAG adds retrieval infrastructure, fine-tuning requires training compute, and pre-training from scratch costs millions. Start at the top and move down only when necessary.

questions.scenario: Which AWS service identifies objects, faces and unsafe content in images and video?
questions.explain: Rekognition analyses images and video. Textract extracts text from documents, Comprehend analyses text meaning, and Kendra provides enterprise search.

questions.scenario: Which term describes the process of using a trained model to generate predictions on new data?
questions.explain: Inference is using the trained model to produce results — cheap and constant. Training is the expensive one-off learning phase. Think of it as migrate versus runserver.

questions.scenario: Which AWS service would be used to build a conversational chatbot with defined intents and slots?
questions.explain: Lex builds conversational interfaces using intents and slots, and is the technology behind Alexa. Polly generates speech, Translate converts languages, and Textract reads documents.

questions.scenario: What is the role of Model Context Protocol (MCP) in agentic AI applications?
options: It provides a standard way for agents to connect to external systems and tools
questions.explain: MCP is a standard for connecting agents to external systems and tools, and is named explicitly in the AIF-C01 exam guide. It is about connectivity, not compression, encryption or evaluation.

questions.scenario: Which responsible AI characteristic refers to a model's outputs being truthful and factually accurate?
questions.explain: Veracity means truthfulness and is one of the responsible AI features the exam lists alongside fairness, inclusivity, robustness and safety. Elasticity, latency and modality are unrelated technical properties.

questions.scenario: Which legal risk is specifically associated with generative AI producing content resembling copyrighted works?
questions.explain: IP infringement is one of the GenAI legal risks the exam guide names, alongside biased outputs, hallucinations and loss of customer trust. The others are operational rather than legal concerns.

questions.scenario: Which service provides a private network connection so that traffic to AWS AI services does not traverse the public internet?
questions.explain: PrivateLink keeps traffic on the AWS network rather than the public internet. CloudFront is a CDN, Artifact provides compliance reports, and Macie discovers sensitive data.

questions.scenario: Which practice helps ensure the origin and history of training data is documented and traceable?
questions.explain: Data lineage and cataloging record where data came from and what happened to it, supporting governance and auditability. The other options have no bearing on data provenance.

questions.scenario: Which inference parameter primarily controls the randomness and creativity of generated output?
questions.explain: Temperature governs randomness: low values produce consistent output, high values more varied and creative results. Max tokens limits length and the context window limits how much input the model sees.

questions.scenario: Which metric is used to evaluate machine translation quality?
questions.explain: BLEU evaluates translation and ROUGE evaluates summarisation. Recall and accuracy are classification metrics rather than generation metrics.

questions.scenario: Which is a genuine business benefit of using AWS managed GenAI services rather than self-hosting models?
options: Lower barrier to entry and faster time to market
No need for any data governance
questions.explain: Managed services lower the barrier to entry and accelerate delivery. Hallucinations are not eliminated by any provider, governance remains a customer responsibility, and usage is billed.

questions.scenario: A retailer wants to recommend products based on customers' past behaviour. Which AWS service is purpose-built for this?
questions.explain: Personalize is the managed recommendation service. Forecast predicts future time-series values, Comprehend analyses text, and Polly generates speech.

questions.scenario: Which service monitors a deployed model for degradation in quality over time?
questions.explain: Model Monitor watches production models for drift and quality degradation. JumpStart provides pre-built models to start with, and Guardrails filters content in Bedrock.

questions.scenario: Which TWO measures directly reduce the risk of prompt injection in a customer-facing GenAI application?
options: Validating and sanitising user input before it reaches the model
Filtering and validating model output before returning it to users
questions.explain: Prompt injection is mitigated the way SQL injection is: never trust user input as instructions, and validate what goes out. Temperature and context window do not affect it, and removing logging would worsen the security posture.

questions.scenario: A model must learn the specialised vocabulary of medical records. Which approach is MOST appropriate?
questions.explain: Domain adaptation through fine-tuning teaches a model a specialist field's language and conventions. Temperature, caching and token limits do not add domain knowledge.

questions.scenario: What does 'context engineering' refer to in foundation model applications?
options: Deliberately assembling the information supplied to the model to improve responses
questions.explain: Context engineering means curating what information the model receives — a concept the exam guide names explicitly. The other options describe unrelated infrastructure concerns.

questions.scenario: Which describes the correct order of stages in a typical AI/ML lifecycle?
options: Data preparation, model training, evaluation, deployment, monitoring
questions.explain: Data comes first, then training, then evaluation, then deployment, then ongoing monitoring and retraining. AIF includes ordering questions with no partial credit, so this sequence is worth knowing exactly.

questions.scenario: What is the primary purpose of reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF)?
options: Aligning model behaviour with human preferences
Compressing the model to run faster
Reducing the number of Regions used
questions.explain: RLHF uses human preference judgements to make model behaviour more helpful and aligned. Compression is distillation, and encryption and Region choice are unrelated.
